notes:
Summary: Ridgeway builds a desktop-first agent assist product sold into mid-market contact centers. Looking to add low-latency streaming suggestions with ticket-side tool-calls (CRM updates, canned-scripts insertion) and on-the-fly ticket summarization for post-call wrap-up. Key ask: sub-100ms suggestion latency for single-agent flows; maintain linear throughput across spikes (50%+ concurrency increase) without degraded suggestion quality or hallucinations.

Recent conversation highlights:
- "Customer wants streaming completion so agents see incremental suggestions as they type — not batched at end." (Product VP)
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs per token, and residency for EU accounts.
- Tooling: integration with their ticket system (ForkTicket) via tool-calls (create/update/attach) and explicit operator confirmations.
- Quality: need guardrails — entity redaction, policy filters, and a rollback flow to human-only responses on uncertain predictions.

POC scope agreed: 2-week evaluation (48-hour continuous spike test inside week 2). Will test dedicated GPU pool with autoscaling and a private control plane for residency. Evaluate streaming latency, fallback to smaller quantized models during overload, and prefix caching effectiveness.

Quote from head of ops: "We can't have suggestions go stale or wrong during peak — risk to CSAT."

Stubs/links: pricing deck in Drive, security FAQ shared, Fireflies transcript for kickoff meeting.

Internal notes (AE/SE): prioritize rollout of canary policy, set model-variant fallback thresholds, instrument token-level tracing for suggestions and tool-call audits.
